topic: how to read a compliance audit finding
text:
When an audit finding lands in your inbox, do not start by reading the recommendation.

Auditors usually build a finding around four core parts: criteria, condition, cause, and effect. Most IT teams look at the condition, panic, and then blindly implement whatever generic remediation the auditor suggested.

That burns engineering time.

The condition is just the snapshot of what failed in the sample. Maybe three offboarded contractors still had active Google Workspace accounts thirty days after leaving. The criteria is your written baseline, like revoking access within 24 hours of separation. The recommendation is often standard boilerplate written by someone who has never touched your identity provider.

Look at the root cause instead.

Did HR send the termination ticket late? Did the ticket sit unassigned in a Jira backlog? Or did your SCIM bridge silently fail on account deactivation because an API token expired?

Those are three completely different operational problems. If you only disable the three accounts and rewrite the policy paragraph to satisfy the report, you treated the symptom. You will fail the exact same sample during the next testing cycle.

Fix the plumbing, not the draft.

When you trace an offboarding finding back to its source, does it usually turn out to be an HR notification failure or an IT queue delay?
